cases.name: Cindy A. Palmer Liquori
cases.about: She was the owner of Cindy's Soap Cottage. Her obituary said, "She had a special talent for decorating and that was shown in the success of her store and in her beautiful home. Cindy had a heart of gold and generosity that showed the type of person she was. Her heart was big, and her smile and laugh would light up a room. She was a great hostess and the "life of the party," and her family and friends will always remember her wonderful Christmas and New Year's Eve parties. To know Cindy was to love Cindy, she was one of a kind."
cases.narrative: She was killed at her mother's house.

cases.name: Delores Tracey Wisdom
cases.about:
She was a volunteer services manager at the Connecticut Food Bank/Foodshare. Jason Jakubowski, president and CEO of the organization, said in a statement. “Delores was more than just our co-worker, she was our friend. She had an energy and a charisma that would light up any room she was in, and her passion for the work that we do was undeniably infectious."

cases.name: Lauren “Lela” Leslie
cases.about:
Her family said she was unapologetically true to who she was, loved to dance, and had a bright future ahead of her. She wanted to pursue physical therapy as a career. 

Jhavier Leslie described his sister as a proud, Black, lesbian woman. “She fought for that. She wasn’t always herself. She had to grow into that, she had to fight for it, through all the prejudice that she went through, people judging her, and the things they would say about her,” Jhavier said. “It doesn’t matter if it was girl clothes or boy clothes, or if she dyed her hair, it was all her, “ he said. Watching her grow up and become proud of who she was gave him strength to fully live his life as well, Jhavier said.
